Ava / team — draft proposal below. Kept it narrowly tailored so it is defensible and avoids opening a large new exposure. Rationale beneath.

--- Proposed replacement for Section 8.2 (Excluded Damages) ---
"Neither party shall be liable to the other for incidental, special, exemplary, consequential or punitive damages arising out of or related to this Agreement, except that the foregoing exclusion shall not apply to: (a) damages resulting from a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (b) claims alleging infringement of a party's intellectual property rights; or (c) Customer's direct loss of Confidential Data caused by Redwood's material breach of its data security obligations. For clarity, \"incidental, special, exemplary, consequential or punitive damages\" does not include direct compensatory damages for: (i) amounts payable under an Order Form; (ii) amounts awarded for proven direct loss of business or lost subscription fees directly attributable to Redwood's breach as set forth in Section 7."

Rationale: 1) Keeps the broad exclusion but creates narrowly drawn carve-outs for gross negligence/willful misconduct and IP/data breach — the two items Acme will push on. 2) Adds clarifying language to preserve direct compensatory remedies that feed into the cap (avoids double counting). 3) Avoids listing examples that could unintentionally expand the definition; instead we exclude certain categories from the exclusion.

Attached: comparison_comments.txt with in-line notes against Acme's redline.

If you agree, I can send to Acme with a short cover note: "We are willing to narrow the exclusion to carve back gross negligence, IP infringement, and direct data-loss where Redwood materially breached security obligations."

-Laura
